purpose: Initial gold-free taxonomy for coding-agent hallucination skill self-evolution.

positive_categories.name: Requirement / intent
positive_categories.definition: Agent misunderstands, omits, or violates explicit issue requirements, acceptance constraints, or user-specified invariants.

positive_categories.name: Repository fact
positive_categories.definition: Agent asserts or relies on a wrong fact about existing files, symbols, helpers, behavior, entry points, configs, data flow, or repo state.

positive_categories.name: API / symbol / dependency
positive_categories.definition: Agent imports, calls, configures, or argues from a nonexistent, unavailable, incompatible, deprecated, or task-forbidden API, package, method, attribute, parameter, command, or tool capability.

positive_categories.name: Resource / path / config
positive_categories.definition: Agent assumes a file path, directory, env var, config key, fixture, dataset, service, permission, or runtime resource exists or is writable/readable when evidence does not support it.

positive_categories.name: Tool observation / execution
positive_categories.definition: Agent misreads, ignores, fabricates, or over-interprets shell output, traceback, grep result, test output, return code, warning, timeout, or partial command result.

positive_categories.name: Structural inconsistency
positive_categories.definition: Agent creates code inconsistent with existing cross-file interfaces, public signatures, type contracts, module boundaries, entry points, config protocols, or call conventions.

positive_categories.name: Patch effect / behavior
positive_categories.definition: Agent claims or relies on a patch effect that is not achieved: public case only, edge case missing, regression introduced, behavior unchanged, or verifier contradicts the claimed effect.

positive_categories.name: Dead / ineffective code
positive_categories.definition: Agent adds or modifies code that appears to be the fix but has no reachable call path, no behavioral contribution, shadowed definition, duplicate implementation, or only cosmetic effect while being treated as a real repair.

positive_categories.name: Completion / progress claim
positive_categories.definition: Agent claims task completion, all tests passing, all edge cases covered, safe submission, or verified progress without sufficient supporting evidence or despite contradicting logs.

positive_categories.name: Documentation / comment
positive_categories.definition: Agent writes or trusts comments, docstrings, README, examples, or explanations that contradict the actual code behavior, API contract, or task requirement.

boundary_states.definition: The agent fails or writes bad code but does not make or rely on an unsupported unit.
The evidence pack cannot establish support or contradiction.
The candidate unit is supported by available evidence.
